Addressing these risks will require a combination of laboratory testing, HIL-based experimentation, and field demonstration. 9.5 Opportunities for Technology Transfer and Industry Impact The modeling tools, metric framework, simulation workflow, and measurement infrastructure developed in BP1 offer broad value to ongoing national efforts to integrate inverter-based resources. Opportunities for technology transfer include: • Using validated GFM metrics and models in utility planning and interconnection studies • Providing OEMs with design guidance for hybrid-plant control strategies • Contributing modeling insights to WECC, IEEE, and NERC working groups • Applying the measurement and validation framework to other renewable hybrid plants Page 28 of 36 Award Number: DE-EE0010651 Recipient Name: Portland General Electric These pathways support industry adoption and align with national priorities for grid reliability under increasing IBR penetration. 9.6 Summary of Path Forward The work completed during BP1 created the analytical, simulation, and engineering foundation necessary for future GFM commissioning and validation. A balanced path forward includes completing field commissioning, validating performance metrics under real system conditions, advancing positive-sequence models, further integrating EMT–HIL workflows, and applying high-resolution measurements for model refinement. Together, these efforts would substantially accelerate the readiness of GFM resources for large-scale deployment and contribute meaningfully to the reliable operation of future inverter-dominated power systems. 10. Products: The project produced a range of technical products and research outputs that support ongoing development, validation, and industry adoption of grid-forming (GFM) technologies. The products generated under this award include the following categories: 10.1 Technical Documents and Reports • Grid-Forming Performance Metrics Document - A detailed definition of quantitative performance metrics for angle stability, frequency response, voltage regulation, current-limiting behavior, and short-circuit characteristics. • Grid Services Definition Document - A stand-alone document defining grid services tailored for the Wheatridge GFM demonstration, including angle strengthening, frequency response, inertia-like behavior, voltage regulation, and grid-strengthening support. • Preliminary Multi-Resource EMT Simulation Study Design - A formal simulation-study design package describing: PSCAD model architecture; test matrix framework, grid events, SCR levels, coupling conditions; Pass/fail criteria and GFM metric extraction. • Preliminary Multi-Resource EMT Interaction Study Results - A results document summarizing GFM BESS, GFM wind, and mixed-resource EMT behavior under multiple grid events, including phase jumps, voltage steps, and weak-grid scenarios. • Hardware-in-the-Loop (HiL) Testbed Development Status Report - A detailed report documenting, including assembly of GFM wind, GFM BESS, and plant- controller hardware in RTDS; Successful integration of PQ meters, amplifiers, and communication interfaces; Preliminary co-simulation results.
